name: Tokyo Haneda Airport
direct_access_note: First-hand browser access to tokyo-haneda.com: 9 pages captured on desktop and mobile, 11 more read with Playwright, 5 interaction scripts; all HTTP 200, no bot challenge. Blocked by the container's network policy (not site defects): www.googletagmanager.com, j.wovn.io and data.wovn.io (translation layer), platinumaps.jp (HANEDA MAP and floor-guide map iframe), search-tokyo-haneda.dga.jp (site-search backend), Zendesk, YouTube, online shop and reservation domains. The interactive map, site-search result quality, chatbot behaviour and external booking flows were therefore not observable, and some Japanese strings seen on English pages may be translated for real users. Scores are expert assessments, not instrumented tests.

steps_to_flight_status_note: International flight from the homepage: International Flights tab, Search by flight number, type the number, search. Domestic flights need 3 (default tab). One more click opens the Sample Plan.
axe_note: Homepage, axe-core WCAG A/AA rule violations. Flight search page: 4 on desktop and mobile (critical 2, serious 2). Special-assistance page: 1 serious.

standouts.name: Flight-specific 'Sample Plan' timeline
standouts.why: Turns a flight number into an ordered journey with counters, gate and outlet recommendations for that terminal, without login.

standouts.name: Real-time congestion and delay panel on the homepage
standouts.why: Delay and cancellation counts, rail service status and car park occupancy in one timestamped block.

standouts.name: Flight cards with status pill, counters, gate and codeshares
standouts.why: All decision-critical fields in one card that reads equally well on mobile; status filters for delayed, cancelled and diverted.

standouts.name: Restaurant and shop search with open-now, coupon, halal and vegetarian filters
standouts.why: Answers real passenger questions and states terminal, floor and before/after security.

standouts.name: Special-assistance content organised by need
standouts.why: Permanent header link; quiet spaces, relay service, Sunflower scheme and an autonomous wheelchair service.

weaknesses: Flight lists do not refresh automatically; saved flights and alerts need the app and a member login
Homepage is about 16 MB with a video hero; lab LCP 24.5 s on throttled mobile
Map and site search depend on third-party hosts and do not degrade gracefully when those are unreachable
Shop, duty-free and parking reservations are spread over many domains with no shared basket or sign-in
News and timetables are often PDFs; no skip link; no security headers on the HTML response
ideas: Make the journey timeline live: update with flight status, add walking times and security waits, and let passengers share it with whoever is collecting them
Offer web alerts (push, WhatsApp, e-mail) without an app install or account
Extend the real-time panel to security and immigration waits and to rail and bus departures
Keep map and search first-party with a list fallback so both work under restrictive networks
Use one basket and one identity for parking, lounge, fast-track and pre-order, surfaced inside the flight timeline
Publish notices as accessible HTML, with PDF as an optional download
gaps: Interactive map (platinumaps.jp), site-search results, chatbot behaviour, route search and online shops not observable
WOVN translation layer was blocked, so residual Japanese strings on English pages may not reflect what users see
Delay, cancellation and diversion status treatments were not live in the sample
App quality and ratings rest on one search result; no store score available
Lighthouse and capture timings are lab values from one container with analytics blocked
